name: Suspicious logarithms
description: Let $$$f$$$($$$x$$$) be the floor of the binary logarithm of $$$x$$$. In other words, $$$f$$$($$$x$$$) is largest non-negative integer $$$y$$$, such that $$$2^y$$$ does not exceed $$$x$$$. Let $$$g$$$($$$x$$$) be the floor of the logarithm of $$$x$$$ with base $$$f$$$($$$x$$$). In other words, $$$g$$$($$$x$$$) is the largest non-negative integer $$$z$$$, such that $$${f(x)}^{z}$$$ does not exceed $$$x$$$. You are given $$$q$$$ queries. The $$$i$$$-th query consists of two integers $$$l_i$$$ and $$$r_i$$$. The answer to the query is the sum of $$$g$$$($$$k$$$) across all integers $$$k$$$, such that $$$l_i \leq k \leq r_i$$$. Since the answers might be large, print them modulo $$${10^9 + 7}$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$q$$$ — the number of queries ($$$1 \leq q \leq 10^5$$$). The next $$$q$$$ lines each contain two integers $$$l_i$$$ and $$$r_i$$$ — the bounds of the $$$i$$$-th query ($$$4 \leq l_i \leq r_i \leq 10^{18}$$$).
output_specification: For each query, output the answer to the query modulo $$$10^9 + 7$$$.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1891D — Suspicious logarithms [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
